title_en: Back ache in the first days of weightlessness
title_ko: 무중력 초기의 허리 통증
text_en: Low back ache or stiffness is common in the first days of weightlessness and was reported in about half of the flights in one large record review. It is usually mild, felt mostly during the sleep period, and typically comes without pain spreading down the leg, numbness or tingling.
text_ko: 무중력에 들어선 첫 며칠 동안에는 허리 통증이나 뻐근함이 흔하며, 한 대규모 의무 기록 검토에서는 검토한 비행의 절반가량에서 보고되었다. 대개 가볍고 주로 수면 시간에 느껴지며, 다리로 뻗치는 통증이나 저림은 보통 동반되지 않는다.

sources.title: Space Adaptation Back Pain: A Retrospective Study (AsMA presentation)
OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C: Spaceflight Experience and Medical Care
Kerstman et al., Space adaptation back pain: a retrospective study

numbers: Back pain in 52% of astronaut flights (382/728); of those affected 86% mild, 11% moderate, 3% severe (Kerstman et al. 2012, abstract only). Lumbar in 86%, present at night in 75% (Kerstman, NTRS 2009). Other sources give 70% (prospective study of 20 astronauts, abstract only) and 68% (1991 survey), so the rate differs between sources.
do_not_claim: That early back pain predicts a later disc herniation (astronaut data found no relation); that the 'mostly mild' split is verified in full text (it comes from an abstract).

title_en: What has eased early back ache in flight
title_ko: 비행 초기 허리 통증을 덜어 준 방법
text_en: For early-flight back ache, curling up with the knees drawn toward the chest and stretching the lower back each helped about nine in ten of those trying them in crew records. General back-pain guidance also favours staying gently active and limiting only the movements that hurt, instead of prolonged bed rest.
text_ko: 비행 초기의 허리 통증에는 무릎을 가슴 쪽으로 끌어당겨 몸을 웅크리는 자세와 허리 스트레칭이 도움이 될 수 있으며, 승무원 기록에서는 시도한 사람 열 명 가운데 아홉 명꼴로 효과를 보았다. 일반적인 허리 통증 관리에서도 오래 누워 쉬기보다는 아픈 동작만 줄이고 가볍게 움직이는 편을 권한다.

key_terms.ko: 무릎을 가슴 쪽으로 끌어당겨 몸을 웅크리는 자세

sources.title: Space Adaptation Back Pain: A Retrospective Study (AsMA presentation)
OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C: Spaceflight Experience and Medical Care
Back pain: diagnosis, treatment and steps to take

numbers: Knees-to-chest position helped 91% and lumbar stretching 90% of those who tried them (Kerstman, NTRS 2009); OCHMO-TB-033 lists positioning, exercises and medication as each at least 85% effective.
do_not_claim: That any position or stretch prevents early back pain (no accepted preventive measure is documented). Medication also appears in the records but is left to the app's medication guide.

title_en: Timing pattern of early-flight back ache
title_ko: 비행 초기 허리 통증이 나타나는 시기
text_en: Adaptation back ache typically begins within the first two days of weightlessness, and in the crew record review none was reported beyond about the twelfth day. It is worth noting the day the pain began, where it sits, and whether it is easing; pain that starts later or follows an injury does not fit this early pattern.
text_ko: 무중력 적응기의 허리 통증은 대개 첫 이틀 안에 시작되며, 승무원 기록 검토에서 비행 열이틀째 이후에는 보고된 사례가 없었다. 통증이 시작된 날과 아픈 자리, 나아지고 있는지를 적어 두면 좋다. 더 늦게 시작되었거나 다친 뒤에 생긴 통증은 이 초기 양상에 들어맞지 않는다.

sources.title: Space Adaptation Back Pain: A Retrospective Study (AsMA presentation)

numbers: Case definition: onset within the first 5 flight days, not triggered by an injury; most cases began within 2 days, prevalence peaked on flight day 2, none reported after flight day 12 (Kerstman, NTRS 2009).
do_not_claim: That pain starting later must be an exercise or suit strain (that reading is a researcher's inference, not a validated criterion).

title_en: Why the back may ache in weightlessness is not settled
title_ko: 무중력에서 허리가 아픈 이유는 아직 확실하지 않다
text_en: Without weight pressing down, the spine straightens and lengthens, so crew members can grow slightly taller in weightlessness. This change may contribute to early back ache, but the cause is not well defined, and weakened trunk muscles have also been proposed.
text_ko: 체중이 실리지 않으면 척추가 곧게 펴지면서 길어지기 때문에 무중력에서는 키가 조금 커질 수 있다. 이런 변화가 비행 초기의 허리 통증에 영향을 줄 수 있지만 원인은 아직 분명히 밝혀지지 않았으며, 몸통 근육이 약해지는 것도 원인 가운데 하나로 거론된다.

sources.title: Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
Risk of Intervertebral Disc Damage evidence book (marked inactive on the HRP evidence index)

numbers: Height can rise by as much as 3% (HRP bone risk page). A six-astronaut MRI study (Bailey et al. 2018, abstract only) tied lumbar flattening and stiffness to multifidus muscle atrophy, not disc swelling, so sources disagree on the mechanism.
do_not_claim: That spinal lengthening or disc swelling is the proven cause of early back pain; that early back pain predicts a disc herniation.

title_en: What a muscle strain is and where it comes from in flight
title_ko: 근육이 늘어나 생긴 통증이란 무엇이며 비행 중 왜 생기는가
text_en: A strain is a muscle or tendon that has been overstretched or partly torn, either by a sudden overload or by repeating the same motion. In spaceflight, joint and muscle pain becomes more frequent because of the exercise equipment and work in the spacesuit.
text_ko: 근육이 늘어나 생긴 통증은 근육이나 힘줄이 지나치게 늘어나거나 일부 찢어진 상태에서 오며, 갑자기 큰 힘이 실리거나 같은 동작을 되풀이할 때 생기기 쉽다. 우주 비행 중에는 운동 기구 사용과 우주복을 입고 하는 선외 활동 때문에 관절과 근육의 통증이 더 잦아진다.

sources.title: Sprains and strains
OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C: Spaceflight Experience and Medical Care

numbers: In astronaut health-surveillance data, strains and sprains were 59% of recorded musculoskeletal injuries and diagnoses, and 6% of all such records were in-flight (HRP evidence report on aerobic capacity and muscle, 2024).
do_not_claim: That in-flight exercise injuries are common in absolute terms (about 0.003 per flight day in one analysis, abstract only); that a wearable can detect a strain.

title_en: Why trips and falls are more likely when gravity returns
title_ko: 중력이 돌아오면 넘어지기 쉬운 이유
text_en: Weightlessness weakens muscles, bones and aerobic fitness, and although daily exercise limits the loss, the amount lost varies widely between people. After landing or on a planetary surface, this can make physical tasks harder and trips, falls and injuries more likely, so new aches after a stumble or heavy task are worth noting.
text_ko: 무중력에서는 근육과 뼈가 약해지고 심폐 체력이 떨어지는데, 매일 운동을 하면 이런 변화를 덜 수 있지만 약해지는 정도는 사람마다 크게 다르다. 그래서 착륙한 뒤나 행성 표면에서는 몸을 쓰는 작업이 더 힘들어지고, 발이 걸리거나 넘어져 다칠 가능성이 커질 수 있다. 헛디딘 뒤나 힘든 작업 뒤에 새로 생긴 통증은 적어 두는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
OCHMO-TB-031: Exercise Overview

numbers: Average loss of strength and aerobic fitness is 10-12% of pre-mission values, and 12-38% of crew (depending on the measure) lose more than 20% (HRP fitness risk page). With current station exercise, peak oxygen uptake fell 7% on average after about 178 days and pre-flight values returned about 30 days after landing (OCHMO-TB-031). Sources differ on bone: one NASA brief calls bone loss 'almost fully mitigated by exercise', CSA says about 1% per month is lost despite exercise.
do_not_claim: That exercise fully prevents muscle or bone loss; any fall or injury rate for Mars gravity (no data).

title_en: First days of care for a strained muscle
title_ko: 근육이 늘어나 아플 때 처음 며칠의 관리
text_en: For a minor strain, stop the movement that hurts instead of pushing through it, rest the area for a day or two, and then build activity back up gradually. Where a cold pack is available, short sessions may ease pain early on, and heat is better left until about three days have passed.
text_ko: 근육이 늘어나 생긴 통증이 가벼울 때는 아픈 동작을 참고 계속하지 말고 멈춘 뒤, 그 부위를 하루 이틀 쉬게 하고 나서 활동을 조금씩 늘리는 것이 좋다. 냉찜질을 할 수 있다면 초기에 짧게 하는 것이 통증을 덜어 줄 수 있으며, 온찜질은 사흘쯤 지난 뒤로 미루는 편이 낫다.

sources.title: Sports injuries: diagnosis, treatment and steps to take

numbers: NIAMS: rest at least a day or two; cold pack for up to 20 minutes at a time, 4 to 8 times a day; no heat for at least 72 hours.
do_not_claim: That raising the limb above the heart or a compression wrap works in weightlessness as on Earth (terrestrial advice; no source adapts it, and cold-pack availability on board was not established). No medicine is suggested here.

title_en: What to recheck after a strain
title_ko: 근육이 늘어나 아픈 뒤 다시 확인할 것
text_en: After a strain, recheck over the next few days whether the pain and any swelling or bruising are shrinking and whether the part still moves and takes load as usual. Pain and swelling that last beyond a few days are a reason to have it assessed.
text_ko: 근육이 늘어나 생긴 통증이 있으면 이후 며칠 동안 통증과 부기, 멍이 줄어드는지, 그 부위를 평소처럼 움직이고 힘을 실을 수 있는지 다시 확인한다. 통증과 부기가 며칠이 지나도 가라앉지 않으면 의료진의 확인을 받아 보는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: Sports injuries: diagnosis, treatment and steps to take
Sprains and strains

do_not_claim: A fixed recheck interval (the source says only 'a few days'); that a wearable signal shows a strain healing.

title_en: When muscle or back pain needs the CMO or ground medical staff
title_ko: 근육이나 허리 통증을 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 알려야 할 때
text_en: Contact the CMO or ground medical staff if pain, swelling or bruising is severe, if the part cannot be moved or loaded, looks deformed or is extremely weak, or if there is numbness or tingling. Back pain after a fall, or with leg weakness, trouble urinating or fever, also needs medical assessment.
text_ko: 통증이나 부기, 멍이 심할 때, 그 부위를 움직이거나 힘을 실을 수 없을 때, 모양이 틀어져 보이거나 힘이 거의 들어가지 않을 때, 저림이 있거나 감각이 둔할 때는 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 알린다. 넘어진 뒤에 허리 통증이 생겼거나, 허리 통증과 함께 다리에 힘이 빠지거나 소변을 보기 어렵거나 열이 날 때도 의료진의 진찰이 필요하다.

sources.title: Sports injuries: diagnosis, treatment and steps to take
Sprains and strains
Back pain

do_not_claim: That an ache without these signs can be left unreported indefinitely; triage tiers beyond this cited list are not sourced.

title_en: Sparing the spine in the first days after landing
title_ko: 착륙 직후 며칠 동안 척추 아끼기
text_en: In astronaut health records, herniated spinal discs have been markedly more frequent in the first year after a mission. One piece of advice drawn from those records is to keep heavy loads off the spine for about the first two days after landing.
text_ko: 우주비행사 건강 기록을 보면 임무를 마친 뒤 첫 한 해 동안 흔히 디스크라고 부르는 추간판 탈출이 눈에 띄게 잦았다. 이 기록을 바탕으로, 착륙 뒤 첫 이틀가량은 척추에 실리는 하중을 되도록 줄이라는 권고가 나와 있다.

sources.title: Scheuring, Musculoskeletal Injuries in US Astronauts (presentation)

numbers: Herniated disc risk 35.9-fold in the first year after a mission, 21.4-fold for cervical discs; a 2009 summit advised minimising axial loading for the first 48 hours after landing (Scheuring, NTRS 2018).
do_not_claim: That early in-flight back pain predicts a later herniation (the same data found no relation); that this risk or the two-day figure has been measured for landing in Mars gravity (the data are from returns to Earth).

title_en: What a drop in activity minutes can and cannot tell
title_ko: 활동 시간이 줄었을 때 알 수 있는 것과 알 수 없는 것
text_en: A drop in recorded activity minutes shows that the day's routine changed, not why. Illness can lower activity, but so can ordinary variation: exercise is scheduled most days, not every day, sessions differ in type and length, and exercise may be skipped on spacewalk days. No wearable signal has been validated as a sign of a strain.
text_ko: 기록된 활동 시간이 줄었다는 것은 그날의 일과가 달라졌다는 뜻일 뿐, 그 이유까지 알려 주지는 않는다. 병이 나도 활동이 줄 수 있지만, 운동이 매일 잡혀 있는 것은 아니고 종류와 길이도 날마다 다르며 선외 활동을 하는 날에는 운동을 거르기도 하므로 평소에도 변동이 있다. 근육이 늘어나 생긴 통증을 알려 준다고 검증된 웨어러블 신호는 없다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: aerobic and muscle
Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
EVA Injury Evidence Report
Radin et al., Harnessing wearable device data for influenza-like illness surveillance

numbers: Exercise is scheduled for 2.5 hours a day including set-up, typically 6 days a week; the treadmill was used on about 47% and the cycle on 37% of mission days (HRP evidence report, 2024). The HRP fitness risk page gives 1.5 hours a day on six to seven days a week and CSA about two hours, so the daily time differs between sources.
do_not_claim: That reduced activity indicates illness, pain or low mood; that a wrist device measures cycling or resistance exercise accurately (it mis-estimated both in one ground study, abstract only, and movement in orbit is mostly arm movement); a single official daily exercise time.

title_en: Eating enough to keep pace with exercise
title_ko: 운동량에 맞춰 충분히 먹기
text_en: In flight, crews have often eaten less than their bodies needed. Eating too little goes with loss of muscle and bone and lower endurance, and exercise adds to the energy required, so meals need to keep pace with training. Limited menu variety can dull appetite, and no wearable signal has been validated as showing an energy shortfall.
text_ko: 비행 중 승무원들은 몸에 필요한 양보다 적게 먹는 일이 많았다. 먹는 양이 모자라면 근육과 뼈가 줄고 지구력이 떨어질 수 있으며, 운동을 하면 필요한 에너지가 더 늘어나므로 운동량에 맞춰 식사도 충분히 하는 것이 좋다. 식단이 단조로워 입맛이 떨어지는 일도 있으며, 에너지 부족을 알려 준다고 검증된 웨어러블 신호는 없다.

sources.title: Smith, Zwart, Douglas, Heer, Human Adaptation to Spaceflight: The Role of Food and Nutrition, 2nd ed.
OCHMO-TB-013 Rev D: Food and Nutrition
Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
Food Evidence Report

numbers: Energy intake averaged about 70% of predicted need from Apollo through Shuttle and about 80% on the station (84% on Expeditions 26-34); body mass loss of 1-5% has been typical, about 2.4% per 100 days on average (Smith et al. 2021; OCHMO-TB-013 Rev D). The food system must supply an average of 3,035 kcal per person per day plus 200 kcal per EVA hour (OCHMO-TB-013 Rev D).
do_not_claim: That every crew under-eats (some Skylab, Mir and recent station crews met their needs); that energy needs are lower in orbit; that under-eating explains a given person's tiredness or slow recovery (sources document endurance, performance and body mass, not subjective fatigue); an individual calorie target.

title_en: Skin complaints are among the most common in orbit
title_ko: 궤도에서 피부 증상은 가장 흔한 증상에 속한다
text_en: Rashes and similar skin complaints have been among the most frequently recorded symptoms on long orbital missions, with many notable episodes starting in the first month. They usually appear as bumps or small scaly patches, with or without redness and itching, and the exact cause is seldom confirmed in flight.
text_ko: 발진을 비롯한 피부 증상은 장기 궤도 임무에서 가장 자주 기록된 증상에 속하며, 오래가거나 되풀이된 사례의 상당수가 첫 달에 시작되었다. 대개 오돌토돌한 돌기나 비늘처럼 일어나는 작은 반점으로 나타나고 붉어짐이나 가려움이 따르기도 하며, 비행 중에 정확한 원인이 확인되는 일은 드물다.

sources.title: Crucian et al., Incidence of clinical symptoms during long-duration orbital spaceflight
Risk of Altered Immune System Responses

numbers: Rash or hypersensitivity: 23 events among 46 crew members over 20.57 flight-years, about 1.1 per flight-year; 18 of 42 'notable' infection- or allergy-type events began in month 1 (Crucian et al. 2016).
do_not_claim: That rashes are '25 times more common in space' (a single-reference comparison flagged by the authors); that a given rash is immune-related, viral or allergic (in-flight labels are presumptive).

title_en: Proposed reasons for rashes in orbit
title_ko: 궤도에서 발진이 생기는 이유로 제시된 것들
text_en: Several contributors to rashes in orbit have been proposed and none is proven. They include cleansers and no-rinse shampoo left on the skin, sweat or damp clothing, low humidity and restricted airflow, the limits of washing without showers or laundry, and changes in immune responses during flight.
text_ko: 궤도에서 발진이 생기는 이유로 여러 가지가 제시되었지만 확실히 밝혀진 것은 없다. 피부에 남은 세정제나 헹구지 않는 샴푸, 땀이나 젖은 옷, 낮은 습도와 원활하지 않은 공기 흐름, 샤워와 세탁을 할 수 없는 위생 여건, 비행 중 면역 반응의 변화가 거론된다.

sources.title: Crucian et al., Incidence of clinical symptoms during long-duration orbital spaceflight
Personal hygiene in space
Risk of Altered Immune System Responses

do_not_claim: That any single factor is the cause of a given rash; that a rash is immune-related or viral without assessment.

title_en: What a wearable can and cannot tell about skin
title_ko: 웨어러블로 피부 상태를 알 수 있는가
text_en: No wearable signal has been validated as a sign of a skin problem. Equipment touching the skin can itself be the trigger: electrodes, masks and suits have been considered as irritants, and contact dermatitis from experiment electrodes has been documented in flight.
text_ko: 피부 문제를 알려 준다고 검증된 웨어러블 신호는 없다. 오히려 피부에 닿는 장비가 원인이 될 수 있는데, 전극과 마스크, 우주복이 자극 요인으로 검토된 바 있고 실험용 전극 때문에 접촉피부염이 생긴 사례가 비행 중에 기록되었다.

sources.title: Crucian et al., Incidence of clinical symptoms during long-duration orbital spaceflight
Law, Gilmore, Kelly, Postflight rash and skin sensitivity following a year-long spaceflight mission

do_not_claim: That a skin temperature or skin conductance reading shows a skin condition; that commercial wrist wearables are documented to cause rashes in orbit (the electrode case is the closest documented example).

title_en: Rubbing and pressure from suits, boots and harnesses
title_ko: 우주복과 부츠, 하네스에 쓸리고 눌려서 생기는 피부 손상
text_en: Gear that presses or rubs can damage the skin. Soft parts of the spacesuit often cause scrapes and bruises at the wrists, arms, knees and ankles, wrinkles in boots can raise blisters, damp gloves are linked to hand and nail injury, and an earlier treadmill harness chafed and bruised shoulders and hips.
text_ko: 피부에 닿아 누르거나 마찰을 일으키는 장비는 피부를 상하게 할 수 있다. 우주복의 부드러운 소재 부분은 손목과 팔, 무릎, 발목에 쓸린 상처와 멍을 자주 남기고, 부츠 안의 주름은 물집을 만들 수 있으며, 장갑 속 습기는 손과 손톱의 손상과 관련이 있다. 예전에 쓰던 트레드밀 하네스는 어깨와 골반 부위를 쓸리고 멍들게 했다.

sources.title: EVA Injury Evidence Report
Glenn Flight Harness

do_not_claim: That suited work caused the rashes in the station record review (timing and location did not point to it there).

title_en: Whether space dries the skin is not settled
title_ko: 우주에서 피부가 건조해지는지는 아직 결론이 없다
text_en: Astronauts have reported dryness, peeling, itching and slow healing of small cuts, mostly on the hands and feet. Yet measurements in a small group in orbit did not show skin moisture or barrier function getting worse, so it is not settled that weightlessness itself dries the skin. The researchers tied the complaints more to washing conditions.
text_ko: 우주비행사들은 주로 손과 발의 피부가 건조하고 벗겨지며 가려움이 있고, 작은 상처가 더디게 아문다고 보고했다. 그러나 궤도에서 소수를 대상으로 한 측정에서는 피부 수분이나 장벽 기능이 나빠지지 않았으므로, 무중력 자체가 피부를 건조하게 하는지는 아직 결론이 나지 않았다. 연구자들은 이런 불편이 우주정거장 환경보다 씻는 여건과 더 관련이 있다고 보았다.

sources.title: Braun, New findings on skin physiological parameters during long-term spaceflight (IAC-18 abstract page)
Braun et al., Current data on effects of long-term missions on the ISS on skin physiological parameters

numbers: Six astronauts self-reported 23 skin symptoms (Braun, IAC-18, 2018); instrument measurements in six astronauts showed no deterioration of hydration or barrier function (Braun et al. 2019, abstract only).
do_not_claim: That weightlessness is proven to dry or thin the skin; that wounds are proven to heal slowly in astronauts (self-reports and animal work only).

title_en: Reducing contact with a likely trigger
title_ko: 원인으로 짐작되는 것과의 접촉 줄이기
text_en: Where a likely trigger can be identified, such as a soap or cleanser, damp clothing, rough fabric, or a strap or sensor resting on the spot, reducing contact with it is a reasonable first step. Avoiding identified irritants is among the measures suggested for persistent skin symptoms in flight.
text_ko: 비누나 세정제, 젖은 옷, 거친 옷감, 그 자리에 닿는 끈이나 센서처럼 원인으로 짐작되는 것이 있으면 먼저 그것과의 접촉을 줄여 보는 것이 무리 없는 첫 단계이다. 비행 중 오래가는 피부 증상에 대해서도 확인된 자극 요인을 피하는 방법이 제시되어 있다.

sources.title: Atopic dermatitis: diagnosis, treatment and steps to take
Crucian et al., Incidence of clinical symptoms during long-duration orbital spaceflight

do_not_claim: That removing a strap or sensor will clear a rash; which product is responsible (testing is often needed). Medicines for skin symptoms are left to the medication guide and the CMO.

title_en: Gentle care for dry or irritated skin
title_ko: 건조하거나 자극받은 피부를 부드럽게 관리하기
text_en: For dry or irritated skin, basic care is gentle: clean with a mild, unscented or non-soap cleanser, pat the skin dry instead of rubbing, and moisturise soon after washing. Try not to scratch or rub the area, and avoid getting overheated.
text_ko: 건조하거나 자극받은 피부는 부드럽게 관리하는 것이 기본이다. 향이 없는 순한 세정제나 비누 성분이 없는 세정제로 닦고, 문지르지 말고 가볍게 두드려 말린 뒤 곧바로 보습제를 바른다. 그 부위를 긁거나 문지르지 않도록 하고 몸이 지나치게 더워지지 않게 한다.

sources.title: Atopic dermatitis: diagnosis, treatment and steps to take

do_not_claim: That these steps (written for eczema care on Earth) have been tested in flight, or which hygiene products are flown. No medicated cream is suggested here.

title_en: Where the rash is and whether it spreads
title_ko: 발진의 위치와 퍼지는지 여부 살펴보기
text_en: Irritation from direct contact tends to stay where the substance touched the skin, while an allergic reaction can spread beyond that spot; the two look alike. So it helps to note where the rash is, whether it matches a contact point, and whether it is spreading or fading over the following days.
text_ko: 직접 닿아서 생긴 자극은 대개 그 물질이 닿은 자리에 머무르지만, 알레르기 반응은 닿은 자리를 넘어 퍼질 수 있고 두 가지는 겉모습이 비슷하다. 그래서 발진이 어디에 있는지, 무언가 닿는 자리와 겹치는지, 며칠 사이에 퍼지는지 가라앉는지를 적어 두면 도움이 된다.

sources.title: Skin exposures and effects

do_not_claim: That location alone tells an irritant reaction from an allergic one (testing is often needed); how soon an allergic reaction appears or how long a rash lasts (no open source in the notes).

title_en: One-sided pain or tingling before a blistering rash
title_ko: 물집성 발진에 앞서 한쪽에만 나타나는 통증이나 저림
text_en: Flight stressors may reawaken dormant viruses such as the one behind shingles. Shingles shows as a painful, usually itchy, blistering rash in a single stripe on one side of the body or face, and pain, itching or tingling in that area can come several days before the rash.
text_ko: 비행 중의 여러 스트레스 요인은 대상포진을 일으키는 바이러스처럼 몸속에 잠복해 있던 바이러스를 다시 활동하게 할 수 있다. 대상포진은 몸이나 얼굴의 한쪽에 띠 모양으로 물집이 잡히는 발진으로 나타나며, 아프고 대개 가렵다. 발진이 나타나기 며칠 전부터 그 자리에 통증이나 가려움, 저림이 올 수 있다.

sources.title: Shingles symptoms
Risk of Altered Immune System Responses

numbers: Shingles blisters scab in 7-10 days and clear in 2-4 weeks (CDC).
do_not_claim: That viral reactivation means the person is ill (shedding is almost always symptom-free); that one-sided tingling is shingles.

title_en: When a rash needs the CMO or ground medical staff
title_ko: 발진을 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 알려야 할 때
text_en: Contact the CMO or ground medical staff about a rash that is severe, does not go away, or comes with other symptoms such as fever. Painful blisters in a band on one side of the body also need assessment, especially on the face, where shingles can threaten vision.
text_ko: 발진이 심하거나, 가라앉지 않거나, 열 같은 다른 증상이 함께 있으면 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 알린다. 몸 한쪽에 띠 모양으로 아픈 물집이 잡힐 때도 진찰이 필요하며, 대상포진이 얼굴에 생기면 시력을 해칠 수 있으므로 더욱 그렇다.

sources.title: Rashes (health topic summary)
sources.publisher: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (NLM-written summary, not the A.D.A.M. encyclopedia)

sources.title: Shingles symptoms
Preventing spread of disease: guidance for cabin crew

do_not_claim: That a rash without these features is harmless. This list is incomplete: signs of skin infection (spreading redness, warmth, pus) and of a severe allergic reaction (face or throat swelling, trouble breathing) had no usable open source in the notes and still need one.

title_en: A stuffy nose is expected in weightlessness
title_ko: 무중력에서 코막힘은 예상되는 변화이다
text_en: In weightlessness body fluid shifts toward the head, and a stuffy nose, a full-feeling head and a puffy face are expected effects that more than half of crew members experience. This congestion is part of adapting to flight and is not, on its own, a sign of infection.
text_ko: 무중력에서는 체액이 머리 쪽으로 쏠리기 때문에 코막힘과 머리가 꽉 찬 느낌, 얼굴 부기가 흔히 나타나며 승무원의 절반 이상이 겪는다. 이런 코막힘은 비행에 적응하는 과정에서 예상되는 변화이며, 그것만으로는 감염의 신호가 아니다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C: Spaceflight Experience and Medical Care
Smith, Zwart, Douglas, Heer, Human Adaptation to Spaceflight: The Role of Food and Nutrition, 2nd ed.

numbers: Head and nose congestion affects more than 50% of crew and is labelled 'space adaptation or CO2-related' (OCHMO-TB-033 Rev C); plasma volume falls about 17% within hours and stays 10-15% below pre-flight (Smith et al. 2021).
do_not_claim: That congestion means infection; that the fluid shift dries the body out or causes a proven early fluid loss (NASA sources conflict); how much cabin carbon dioxide contributes (asserted, not quantified).

title_en: Congestion is common in the records; infections are rare
title_ko: 기록상 코막힘은 흔하고 감염은 드물다
text_en: In space station health records, a blocked nose was logged for about three in four astronauts, while ear, nose and throat infections were recorded for only a few. Congestion therefore should not be read as infection, although the records offer no tested way to tell the two apart.
text_ko: 우주정거장 건강 기록에서 코막힘은 우주비행사 네 명 가운데 세 명꼴로 기록되었지만, 귀와 코, 목의 감염이 기록된 사람은 몇 명에 그쳤다. 따라서 코막힘을 곧 감염으로 받아들여서는 안 되며, 다만 이 기록에는 둘을 가려내는 검증된 방법이 제시되어 있지 않다.

sources.title: Khan et al., Congestion and sinonasal illness in outer space
Crucian et al., Incidence of clinical symptoms during long-duration orbital spaceflight

numbers: Of 71 station astronauts (2000-2019), 53 (75%) had congestion recorded, 597 instances; ear-nose-throat infections 5 entries in 2 astronauts, sinusitis 1 entry (Khan et al. 2025). An earlier review counted 20 events of prolonged congestion, rhinitis or sneezing against 1 of sore throat (Crucian et al. 2016).
do_not_claim: That congestion means infection; that infections never occur in flight; any rule that separates the two from symptoms or wearable data.

title_en: How congestion usually changes over a mission
title_ko: 임무 기간에 따른 코막힘의 변화
text_en: Recorded congestion was most frequent in the first week of flight and dropped sharply in the second, but entries continued late into missions, which may point to other triggers. It helps to note when stuffiness began and whether anything new, such as a sore throat, cough or fever, has joined it.
text_ko: 기록된 코막힘은 비행 첫 주에 가장 많았다가 둘째 주에 뚜렷이 줄었지만, 임무 후반까지도 이어져 다른 유발 요인이 있을 가능성이 제기된다. 코막힘이 언제 시작되었는지, 인후통이나 기침, 열 같은 새로운 증상이 더해졌는지를 적어 두면 도움이 된다.

sources.title: Khan et al., Congestion and sinonasal illness in outer space
About common cold

numbers: Week 1 had the most events (107), with a sharp fall in week 2; the mean flight day of an event was 70, median 61 (Khan et al. 2025).
do_not_claim: That late-mission congestion is an infection or an allergy; a validated symptom rule for telling fluid-shift congestion from a cold.

title_en: What a cold is and how it spreads in a closed cabin
title_ko: 감기란 무엇이며 밀폐된 선내에서 어떻게 옮는가
text_en: A cold is a viral infection of the nose and throat that can bring a runny or blocked nose, sneezing, cough, sore throat, mild aches and, in adults, usually only a low fever. It spreads through droplets from coughs and sneezes, contaminated hands and surfaces and close contact, and microbes pass between people more easily in a closed habitat.
text_ko: 감기는 코와 목에 생기는 바이러스 감염으로, 콧물이나 코막힘, 재채기, 기침, 인후통, 가벼운 몸살 기운이 나타날 수 있고 성인은 열이 나더라도 대개 미열에 그친다. 기침과 재채기로 튀는 침방울, 오염된 손과 표면, 가까운 접촉을 통해 옮으며, 밀폐된 거주 공간에서는 미생물이 사람 사이에 더 쉽게 옮겨 간다.

sources.title: About common cold
Hazard: Hostile/Closed Environments
The Human Body in Space

numbers: More than 200 viruses can cause a cold, rhinoviruses most often (CDC).
do_not_claim: That cold-like symptoms in flight are a cold (in-flight diagnosis is rarely confirmed); that symptoms alone separate a cold from flu.

title_en: The usual course of a cold
title_ko: 감기의 일반적인 경과
text_en: Cold symptoms usually peak within two to three days and are mostly gone in under a week. It is worth tracking each day whether symptoms are easing, whether there is fever and how long it lasts, and whether symptoms that had improved come back.
text_ko: 감기 증상은 대개 이삼일 안에 가장 심해지고 일주일이 되기 전에 대부분 가라앉는다. 증상이 나아지고 있는지, 열이 있는지와 며칠째 이어지는지, 좋아지던 증상이 다시 나빠지는지를 날마다 확인해 두는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: About common cold
Common cold treatment

do_not_claim: That a higher temperature reading in orbit equals fever (resting temperature drifts upward in flight); that a cold as a rule turns into a bacterial infection.

title_en: Why infections are uncommon in flight but still possible
title_ko: 비행 중 감염이 드물지만 생길 수는 있는 이유
text_en: Before launch, crews spend about two weeks in isolation and are immunised, mainly to keep airway and gut infections off the vehicle. This lowers the risk but cannot remove it, and some astronauts have still become ill in space; before such isolation existed, colds spread through whole crews.
text_ko: 발사 전 승무원은 두 주가량 격리 생활을 하고 예방접종을 받는데, 주로 호흡기와 장의 감염이 우주선에 들어오지 않게 하려는 것이다. 이렇게 하면 위험이 낮아지지만 완전히 없앨 수는 없어서 우주에서 병이 난 우주비행사도 있었다. 이런 격리가 없던 시절에는 감기가 승무원 전원에게 퍼진 적이 있다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-006 Rev C: Health Stabilization Program
Risk of Host-Microorganism Interactions

numbers: The health stabilization programme starts 14 days before launch; the incubation period of almost all relevant infections is three weeks or less; before it existed 57% of Apollo crew members had an infectious illness before flight, and all three crew of Apollo 7 and of Apollo 9 had colds (OCHMO-TB-006 Rev C).
do_not_claim: That quarantine guarantees no infection; that astronauts are 'immunocompromised' (in-flight immune changes are described as mostly not needing treatment).

title_en: Limiting spread to crewmates
title_ko: 동료에게 옮기지 않기
text_en: A cold passes on through coughs and sneezes, hands, shared surfaces and close contact. When someone has cold-like symptoms, the measures used in pre-launch isolation can be applied on board as far as the cabin allows: clean hands often, cover coughs and sneezes, and keep some distance from crewmates.
text_ko: 감기는 기침과 재채기, 손, 함께 쓰는 표면, 가까운 접촉을 통해 옮는다. 그래서 감기 같은 증상이 있을 때는 발사 전 격리에서 쓰는 방법대로 손을 자주 닦고, 기침과 재채기를 가리고, 선내 여건이 되는 만큼 동료와 거리를 두는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-006 Rev C: Health Stabilization Program
About common cold

do_not_claim: That these measures are documented in-flight practice (the source describes pre-launch measures); that they prevent transmission in a small shared cabin.

title_en: Basic care for cold-like symptoms
title_ko: 감기 같은 증상이 있을 때의 기본 관리
text_en: A cold usually clears by itself, and the basics of care are rest and plenty of fluids. Medicines can ease symptoms but do not cure a cold, and which ones to use is for the medication guide and the CMO.
text_ko: 감기는 대개 저절로 낫고, 관리의 기본은 휴식과 충분한 수분 섭취이다. 약은 증상을 덜어 줄 수는 있어도 감기 자체를 낫게 하지는 않으며, 어떤 약을 쓸지는 약물 안내와 CMO의 판단에 따른다.

sources.title: Common cold treatment
About common cold

do_not_claim: That steam, humidifiers or sprays suit a spacecraft cabin (terrestrial advice; no source adapts it to weightlessness); that any medicine is appropriate for a given crew member.

title_en: When cold-like symptoms need the CMO or ground medical staff
title_ko: 감기 같은 증상을 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 알려야 할 때
text_en: Contact the CMO or ground medical staff if there is trouble breathing or fast breathing, fever lasting more than four days, symptoms that go beyond ten days without improving, symptoms that improve and then return or worsen, or signs of running low on fluids. Fever together with a rash or a persistent cough should also be reported.
text_ko: 숨쉬기가 힘들거나 숨이 가빠질 때, 열이 나흘 넘게 이어질 때, 증상이 열흘이 지나도 나아지지 않을 때, 좋아지던 증상이 다시 나타나거나 더 나빠질 때, 몸에 수분이 모자란 징후가 보일 때는 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 알린다. 열과 함께 발진이나 계속되는 기침이 있을 때도 알려야 한다.

sources.title: Common cold treatment
Preventing spread of disease: guidance for cabin crew

numbers: CDC: fever lasting longer than 4 days; symptoms lasting more than 10 days without improving. CDC's cabin-crew definition of fever is a measured 38 C (100.4 F) or higher, feeling warm to the touch, or a history of feeling feverish.
do_not_claim: A numeric fever cut-off applied to a wearable reading (resting temperature drifts upward in orbit); that early-mission stuffiness alone needs escalation.

title_en: Body temperature runs higher in orbit
title_ko: 궤도에서는 체온이 더 높게 나온다
text_en: Resting body temperature drifts upward over the first months in orbit and rises higher and faster during exercise than on Earth. A reading compared with a pre-flight baseline can therefore look raised without any illness, so a higher reading in orbit is not, by itself, a fever.
text_ko: 궤도에서는 안정 시 체온이 첫 몇 달에 걸쳐 조금씩 올라가고, 운동할 때는 지상에서보다 더 높이 더 빨리 오른다. 그래서 비행 전 기준선과 비교하면 아프지 않아도 체온이 높아진 것처럼 보일 수 있으며, 궤도에서 측정값이 높다는 것만으로는 열이 난다고 볼 수 없다.

sources.title: Stahn et al., Increased core body temperature in astronauts during long-duration space missions

numbers: Resting core temperature rose gradually by about 1 C over 2.5 months in orbit (Stahn et al. 2017, abstract only).
do_not_claim: That a higher temperature reading in orbit equals fever; that wrist skin temperature tracks core temperature in flight (no astronaut data); a numeric fever threshold for wearable readings.

title_en: What wearable signals can and cannot tell about infection
title_ko: 웨어러블 신호로 감염을 알 수 있는가
text_en: In studies on Earth, infection has been linked with a higher resting heart rate and higher skin temperature, but the accuracy for spotting illness in one person varied widely. None of this evidence comes from astronauts, and no wearable signal has been validated for telling a cold from ordinary congestion.
text_ko: 지상 연구에서는 감염이 있을 때 안정 시 심박수와 피부 온도가 높아지는 경향이 보고되었지만, 한 사람의 감염 여부를 알아내는 정확도는 연구마다 크게 달랐다. 이런 근거 가운데 우주비행사에게서 얻은 것은 없으며, 감기와 평소의 코막힘을 구별해 준다고 검증된 웨어러블 신호는 없다.

sources.title: Mitratza et al., Performance of wearable sensors in the detection of SARS-CoV-2 infection
Radin et al., Harnessing wearable device data for influenza-like illness surveillance

numbers: Model accuracy for detecting SARS-CoV-2 ranged from 0.52 to 0.92 (area under the curve) and pre-symptomatic detection from 20% to 88% of cases (Mitratza et al. 2022, abstract only).
do_not_claim: That a wearable can diagnose a cold or fever; that a raised heart rate or temperature reading indicates infection (exercise, stress, poor sleep and the in-orbit temperature drift give the same pattern).

title_en: Drinking enough, with or without a cold
title_ko: 감기가 있든 없든 물을 충분히 마시기
text_en: In flight, people often drink less than before launch and less than recommended, possibly because thirst is blunted, so thirst may be a poor prompt. Drinking too little raises the chance of kidney stones, and a larger fluid shortfall can impair concentration and coordination. Plenty of fluids is also part of basic care for a cold.
text_ko: 비행 중에는 발사 전보다, 그리고 권장량보다 물을 적게 마시는 일이 흔한데, 갈증을 덜 느끼기 때문일 수 있어 목이 마를 때만 마셔서는 모자랄 수 있다. 수분 섭취가 적으면 신장 결석이 생길 가능성이 커지고, 수분 부족이 심하면 집중력이 떨어지고 몸놀림이 둔해질 수 있다. 감기 증상이 있을 때에도 물을 충분히 마시는 것이 기본 관리에 들어간다.

key_terms.en: low fluid level in the body

sources.title: Smith, Zwart, Douglas, Heer, Human Adaptation to Spaceflight: The Role of Food and Nutrition, 2nd ed.
Hazard: Gravity Fields
Common cold treatment

numbers: By urine concentration about 40% of station astronauts met a sports-medicine definition of low hydration and 8.7% a clinical one; impairment is described once the water deficit passes about 2% of body mass; water intake on Expeditions 26-34 averaged about 2.3 kg a day (Smith et al. 2021; OCHMO-TB-013 Rev D).
do_not_claim: That weightlessness by itself dries the body out (NASA sources conflict on early fluid loss); a daily water target (only suited-operations minimums and observed intakes were verified); that a wearable shows fluid status.
